identifier: Why we ask for personal information
statement: As you continue the process of signing up for WooPayments, we’ll ask for information about your business, including the business owner’s date of birth and tax ID number.

identifier: Why do I have to share this information?
statement: Before we build a payment relationship with a customer, we ask for the information listed above to validate the business owner’s identity and tax ID number, and to ensure that we can connect the listed bank account with the business itself.

identifier: How quickly will you confirm my identity?
statement: Typically, we’ll confirm your application within a couple of days.

identifier: What else should I keep in mind?
statement: If you’re setting up WooPayments for someone else, it’s best to have that person complete the account creation process.

identifier: What else should I keep in mind?
statement: It’s not always possible to change account information once it’s been saved, especially if the site accepts live transactions before the correct account information is entered.

identifier: Signing up for WooPayments: Before you begin
statement: Be sure to select the correct country for your account, as it cannot be changed later.
Provide the required business information and select Continue. Verify your business details with our payments partner, Stripe.

identifier: The WooPayments signup process: Test payments
statement: Note: Selecting Test payments will create a test account, which will allow you to safely test payments in a sandbox-like environment. However, you cannot accept real payments with a test account.
Note that the phone number you provide during signup also becomes your store’s support phone number, which is semi-public business contact info.
After you’re done signing up, you may see a notice on the Payments > Overview page that your account information is under review:
This is normal, and the notice will go away once your information is verified.
When you’re ready to go live, remember to disable test mode before accepting live payments.

identifier: What if a payment method can’t be enabled?
statement: Depending on your account status, certain payment methods may be unavailable, and you’ll be asked to contact support to enable them.

identifier: Alipay and WeChat Pay additional requirements
statement: Before enabling Alipay or WeChat Pay, make sure your website is complete, publicly accessible, and accurately reflects the products or services you offer.

identifier: Alipay and WeChat Pay additional requirements
statement: Your site must be live and not under construction or password-protected. All listed products or services should be visible and clearly described.

identifier: Alipay and WeChat Pay additional requirements
statement: This requirement comes from Alipay and WeChat Pay’s review process and applies to all merchants. Enabling these payment methods before your website is ready may result in approval delays or even rejection.

identifier: Alipay and WeChat Pay prohibited businesses
statement: If your business falls into one of the prohibited categories below, your request to enable the payment method will be rejected, and re-applying will not change the outcome.

identifier: Alipay and WeChat Pay approval delays
statement: Alipay and WeChat Pay are subject to approval delays of up to five business days after being enabled in WooPayments. During this time, these payment methods may not appear at checkout, even if they are turned on in your settings.
